physicalNotes: Radius 8.963 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17608: radius 7.747 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 211.434 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.783) and temperature; scaled from the paper's distance, 116.55 pc, to the cluster's, 134.84 pc: at a fixed temperature the radius grows with the distance, so 7.747 x 134.84/116.55 = 8.963 solar radii (luminosity 283.0) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 6,235,559 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 7913 +/- 3358 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17608: effective temperature 7913 +/- 3358 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.448) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
